original.title: A complete criterion for the specified charged bounded-shell certificate class
original.statement: For a fixed eventual rail mask and cap table, the exact residual Hall union yields a sufficient local inequality n−A_v>D_J(v,n;A). Initial cut intervals lose no generality in this specified charged class, and least successful terminal cuts require no extra equality charge.
assumptions: Precisely specified mask, cap table, allowed same-shell jump J and full I/II coverage. Completeness is for this class only, not all proof grammars.

exactAuditedStatement: In the specified charged bounded-shell class, with all I/II replies covered and typeIII same-shell jumps>J charged, largest cut n has exact residual union D_J=#{ell<k hole:A_ell<n}+#{ell<k hole:A_ell=n, k-ell>J}. A_v+1,..., n cuts are certified by n-A_v>D_J. Any successful cut subset normalizes to an initial interval; a least successful terminal has no far equality charge.
hypotheses: Fixed periodic rail mask, positive cap A_v, common zero cap M; positive-lag terminal n<=M; lag zero terminal M+1.
This is exact for prescribed overcount/coverage class, not a necessary condition for all Chomp proofs.
proofDependencyMap: Complete bottom-cut reply families (independently derived in legacy124).
Precise raw support conditions read in charged_prune.py: for j<n, cap(k+j, phase-j)>=n-j or rail; face caps>=n-d.
independentDerivationAndChecks: At cut u, unresolved III lower lag ell occurs iff A_ell<u, or A_ell=u and k-ell>J. Taking union for u<=n gives exactly the two sets displayed: interior far equality cap u<n is already in first set. Every lower lag can provide at most one P across cuts because same top/middle with different bottoms are mutually reachable. Distinct N cut neighbors require one P each and no one P can be a reply for two different cut bottoms. Thus more cuts than residual lags is contradiction.

The largest cut n already contains every lag with cap<n; adding missing interior cuts does not add new union members. I/II coverage at n implies coverage at lower u: the parameter ranges shrink and required child ages u-j/u-d decrease. Hence initial cut intervals lose no generality in this class.

As n increases, near contributions switch at cap n-1 and far at cap n, so D(n)-D(n-1)=#near(cap n-1)+#far(cap n)>=0. If success at n includes a far equality charge, increment>=1 and(n-1)-A_v>D(n-1). This automatically requires n-1>A_v, since RHS nonnegative. Support is monotone easier at n-1, contradicting least success.

Supporting pruning proof: growing child caps weakens charged indicators and enlarges support. Therefore any certificate C below A survives T(A). Descending finite integer updates reach a fixed point preserving every C. Rank box and shaving need their class specific support conditions; no computed C460no72claim is an input to the local theorem.

Uniform shaving by c retains n-c>0, for which(A_ell-c)_+<n-c iff A_ell<n, and equality iff A_ell=n. This justifies normalization with the stated positive cap guard. The recorded numeric C460 obstruction is a separate certificate claim; this catalogue statement is the local criterion, proved without trusting those search counts.
